[[File:St Pete Times Forum At Sunset.jpg|thumb|300px|right|The Lightning have played their home games at Benchmark International Arena since 1996.]]
The [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] are an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Tampa, Florida]]. They play in the [[Atlantic Division (NHL)|Atlantic Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). Often referred to as the Bolts,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lightning.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=394050 |title=Lightning Unveil Third Jerseys vs. Devils |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |date=2008-11-23 |accessdate=2008-12-21 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081227211443/http://lightning.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=394050 |archivedate=2008-12-27 }}</ref> the team joined the NHL in 1992 as an [[expansion team]], and have won the [[Stanley Cup]] [[List of Stanley Cup champions|championship]] in 2004, 2020 and 2021.<ref name="cup"/> Having first played in the [[Expo Hall]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lightning.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=7084|title=1992-93 The Fun Begins|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2008-12-21|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081217182004/http://lightning.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=7084|archivedate=2008-12-17}}</ref> and later in the ThunderDome (now known as [[Tropicana Field]]),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tampabay.rays.mlb.com/tb/ballpark/ballpark_history.jsp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071111181648/http://tampabay.rays.mlb.com/tb/ballpark/ballpark_history.jsp|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 11, 2007|title=Tropicana Field History|publisher=MLB Advanced Media, L.P|work=[[MLB.com]]|accessdate= 2008-12-21}}</ref> the Lightning have played their home games at the Ice Palace, currently titled [[Benchmark International Arena]], since 1996. The Lightning are owned by [[Jeffrey Vinik]], [[Julien BriseBois]] is their [[general manager]], and [[Victor Hedman]] is the team [[Captain (ice hockey)|captain]].

There have been nine&nbsp;[[head coach]]es for the Lightning franchise. The team's first head coach was [[Terry Crisp]], who coached for five seasons. [[John Tortorella]], the only [[United States|American]] to head coach the team, was the first Lightning coach to have won the [[Prince of Wales Trophy]],<ref name="powt"/> the [[Stanley Cup]],<ref name="cup"/> and to have been awarded the [[Jack Adams Award]], all of which happened in the [[2003–04 NHL season|2003–04 season]]. [[Rick Paterson]], [[Steve Ludzik]] and [[Jon Cooper (ice hockey)|Jon Cooper]] are the only ones who have spent their entire NHL head coaching careers with the Lightning.

[[Jon Cooper (ice hockey)|Jon Cooper]] is the team's current head coach, having been named to the position on March 25, 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://lightning.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=662090 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130329101527/http://lightning.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=662090 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 29, 2013 |title=Lightning name Jon Cooper as head coach |date=March 25, 2013 |work=Lightning.nhl.com |accessdate=March 25, 2013}}</ref> Cooper is the only head coach of the Lightning to win the [[Prince of Wales Trophy]] four times.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/page.htm?id=24967|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110901190807/http://www.nhl.com/ice/page.htm?id=24967|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 1, 2011|title=Prince of Wales Trophy|publisher=The National Hockey League|work=[[National Hockey League|NHL]]|accessdate=2022-08-02}}</ref> Under Cooper, the franchise won its second [[Stanley Cup]] championship in [[2020 Stanley Cup Finals|2020]] and third championship in [[2021 Stanley Cup Finals|2021]]. Cooper is the franchise's all-time leader for the most regular season wins (572), playoff games coached (155), and the most playoff-games won (888).
